public_rationale: Anthropic's October 26, 2026 filing warned that insufficient revenue growth or financing could leave it unable to meet compute obligations [e1]. The passage describes a risk; it does not document a qualifying capacity delay or an inability to pay caused by one [e1]. It supplies no corresponding outcome evidence for OpenAI, leaving the conditional forecast unresolved [e1].
limitations: The passage does not establish original delivery schedules, actual availability dates, payment triggers or settlement of affected obligations [e1].
The risk warning establishes neither actual payment failure nor the absence of payment difficulties [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If compute capacity doesn't come online fast enough, OpenAI and Anthropic will not be able to pay for it.
conditions: if compute capacity doesn't come online fast enough

statement.excerpt: If capacity doesn’t come on fast enough, OpenAI and Anthropic can’t pay for it.

from_speaker: If capacity doesn’t come on fast enough
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that delayed compute availability prevents the labs from generating or obtaining enough money to meet their compute obligations.
A qualifying delay must be measured against the delivery schedule underlying the affected lab's obligations. General capacity shortages alone do not establish this condition.
The statement names both companies. Full support requires evidence for both; evidence concerning only one cannot establish the entire claim.
The surrounding discussion of 2027 spending does not supply a deadline for this particular conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Verified capacity delays cause both labs to become unable to meet the affected compute payment obligations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying delayed-capacity episode concludes with an affected lab demonstrably able to meet all associated obligations despite the delay, contradicting the claimed necessary inability to pay.

evidence.explanation: Anthropic identifies the risk that revenue will not cover its commitments. This is a prospective warning, not evidence that a delivery delay occurred or caused either lab to become unable to pay.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Delivery schedules, availability dates and financial records showing that qualifying delays caused both labs to become unable to meet the affected compute obligations. Alternatively, a completed delayed-capacity episode with all associated obligations settled by an affected lab would provide a counterexample.
